To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) stover yield and its quality traits are important for forage/biofuel production utility in high-oil dent maize; 2) QTL mapping of stover yield and related quality traits in two connected populations with different genetic backgrounds showed the importance of environments and genetic background in stover QTL detection; 3) common QTL among traits are consistent with their correlation.
the genetic basis of yield and quality traits in stover portion is complex, and QTL detected herein are consistent with their correlations and previous researches.
the QTL for stover traits in high-oil dent maize were detected using two connected populations, and the results were affected by environments and genetic backgrounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first report of QTL mapping for stover yield traits in high-oil dent maize.

the genetic architecture of stover traits and the genetic basis for their correlations, and provides valuable information for further genetic dissection of the stover traits and their genetic improvement.
the genetic control of stover yield and its quality traits in maize and provides a useful reference for further researches in this field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QTL detection for yield and quality traits of maize stover was influenced by genetic backgrounds and environments.
the genetic basis of stover yield and its quality traits is complex and that the genetic architecture of these traits is influenced by the genetic backgrounds and environments.
the genetic architecture of the stover traits was complex and that QTL mapping was a useful tool to detect the genetic loci for stover traits in maize.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QTL mapping for stover yield or quality traits was feasible and effective in high-oil dent maize.
QTL detection for yield and quality traits was feasible, and the detected QTL would be useful for marker-assisted selection in breeding for forage and biomass maize.

the QTL detection for yield and quality traits in maize stover is complex and environment dependent, and the genetic basis of stover yield and composition traits are different from those of grain yield and composition traits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QTL detection results are highly dependent on the genetic backgrounds and environments.
QTL mapping for stover traits is feasible and can be conducted in connected populations.
the genetic control of stover traits in high-oil and normal-oil maize is complex, and the detected QTL will be useful for marker-assisted breeding for high-oil and high-stover yield maize.
